title: Forward Engine Mount Heat Shield and Link Bushing Change for Extended Bushing Life
abstract: Launched change to the forward engine mount heat shield and link bushings, extending bushing life on aircraft with high thrust reverser usage where radiated heat is degrading the bushing liner.

sections.reason: Forward mount link bushings are being found with a degraded liner at engine removal on about one aircraft in five, well before the published inspection interval, and the pattern follows thrust reverser usage rather than flight hours. Fifty-two findings were recorded over three years, concentrated on aircraft operating into short runways where the reverser is used at high power on almost every landing. Temperature survey work on two aircraft showed the bushing running forty degrees above the design assumption during a full reverse selection, which the delivered heat shield does not address because it was sized for the steady cruise case.
sections.description: The forward mount heat shield CAD50991-63 is replaced by a deeper item that wraps the link ends, and the shroud D7120114517025 and its left-hand variant TR739331-85 are re-issued so that the shield can be installed without removing the mount. The nozzle kit D7120115408026 at the bleed pass-through is re-positioned to clear the deeper shield. The link bushings themselves are changed to a liner qualified to a higher continuous temperature. Tension bolts AES840808-93 and titanium bolts LN569360-2A are renewed at every installation. Functional items 395EN and 5598PP are affected. Work is in the nacelle and pylon at zones 423, 443 and 431. Reference detail is on drawings D71201159220 and D71201188098.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 2.2 kg per engine. No electrical load change. The heat shield is not interchangeable with the delivered item because the link end clearance changes, and the bushing is interchangeable in both directions. The bushing inspection interval is expected to extend from six thousand to fourteen thousand cycles once the change is embodied, which is the whole commercial case. Maintenance manual content for the mount inspection changes and the illustrated parts figure needs a pre and post modification pair for the shield.
sections.embodiment_note: Design has started. Production cut-in is intended at the next nacelle standard change and there is no retrofit bulletin planned, because the change is done naturally at engine removal and the operators most affected remove engines often. Spares will be supplied in the new standard only.
sections.open_points: Detailed design must settle whether the deeper shield clears the pylon bleed duct route on aircraft at the later isolation valve standard, and whether the temperature survey has to be repeated with the shield fitted before the interval extension can be claimed.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in intended at the next nacelle standard change; no retrofit bulletin planned
